newsitem.title: UK: Dorrell says Hague offers UK Conservatives change.
newsitem.headline: Dorrell says Hague offers UK Conservatives change.

text.p: Stephen Dorrell, a long-shot in the race for the Conservative leadership, appeared on Friday to boost the chances of front-runner William Hague by saying he could provide the party with a clean break with the past.

Six former cabinet ministers are seeking to succeed John Major as leader in an election expected to be held next month among the ragged band of 164 members of parliament who survived the party's battering by the voters in the May 1 election.

But Dorrell told his first election news conference that only he and Hague could offer the chance of putting aside the internal arguments which contributed heavily to the party's poor performance at the polls.

"In the leadership election two candidates offer the party the opportunity to move on by both changing generation and at the same time breaking free of the arguments which have so damaged the party in recent years," he said.
"William Hague and I not only offer the party that opportunity; we both advocate it," Dorrell, the former health secretary, said.
Dorrell challenged Hague, who at 36 is by far the youngest of the six candidates, to a debate which he said would "allow the party to make an informed choice between us".

Dorrell denied that his warm words about Hague meant that should he be forced to withdraw from the election process because he received low support in the first round of voting he would urge his supporters to transfer their allegiance to Hague.
"No, I am not saying that," he said in answer to a question.

Bookmakers William Hill make Hague 4-7 on to win the leadership, with former finance minister Kenneth Clarke the second favourite at 4-1. Dorrell is the longest-priced of the declared candidates at 14-1.

Dorrell called at his news conference for a thorough review of the party's constitution so that in future all party members, not just MPs, would be involved in the election of the leader. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
